items.question: PAIRED RULING - ONE seam, raised independently from both sides: close the P10-012 unit at 29:19 and open the P10-013 unit at 29:20 (instead of the current 29:20|29:21 seam). Rule the pair as ONE decision: ADOPT the seam move with both rows' exact new spans + tiling consequence, or DECLINE for both. A split verdict (adopt one side only) is incoherent - forbidden.

P10-012.challenge_claim: At the juncture the row declares undecided it discloses the mark at 29:15 without its direction while reading the same layer as closing at 29:20; a second formula object and a rival onset inside the span go unquoted; and two paseq segs in the span are undisclosed while the ketiv/qere in one of those verses is disclosed.
P10-012.grounds: All four arms verify. Direction: the field says a setumah closes the span at oshb:Jer.29.20 but says only that a setumah sits in the opening verse oshb:Jer.29.15; under the closing reading applied one clause earlier, the 29:15 seg divides 29:15 from 29:16 and is weak single-witness corroboration for the very alternative the row declares unsettled. The weight stays tier-3 and never a driver - the defect is the asymmetric disclosure at the crux, not the weight. Second object: oshb:Jer.29.16 opens the bare shape, which the row does quote, while oshb:Jer.29.17 opens כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (byte tier), koh-amar with tsevaot and without the Elohei-Yisrael element - a distinct count object (sweep: 50 verses carry the tsevaot-headed shape, skeleton tier; 29:17 is a member and 29:16 is not) - and it is undisclosed. Rival onset: the span's own last verse opens וְאַתֶּ֖ם שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה (byte tier), the plural hear-the-word-of-YHWH summons with a vocative naming the exiles (sweep: 10 verses book-wide, skeleton tier), standing immediately after 29:19, which carries the closure formula twice and ends on it verse-finally; that puts a live tier-1 seam at 29:19/29:20 which the row never weighs, while it does weigh 29:20/29:21. Marks: paseq segs stand at MT 29:16 and MT 29:18 inside the span, both undisclosed, while the ketiv/qere at MT 29:18 is disclosed - a one-layer omission inside a verse the row already cites. The parashah marks at MT 29:15 and MT 29:20 match the inventory under their claimed types, and all four English quotations in the field are verbatim against the staged text.
P10-012.remedy: device_notes: state the 29:15 seg with the same closing direction used at 29:20, adding that under that reading it corroborates - weakly, single-witness - joining 29:15 to what precedes; and add the paseq segs at MT 29:16 and MT 29:18 (single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position claimed). boundary_rationale: quote the tsevaot-headed formula at 29:17 and name it as its own count object. strongest_rejected_alternative: weigh the 29:19/29:20 juncture, naming the summons shape at 29:20 and the doubled verse-final closure at 29:19. PROPOSAL only, requiring explicit adoption and never author work: close this unit at 29:19 and open the next at 29:20 - the same seam raised independently against the unit that begins at 29:21. Tests: the span's mark-disclosure sweep must return no undisclosed seg in any layer; every formula cited must name its own count object; and the corrected rejection must survive a byte read of oshb:Jer.29.19 and oshb:Jer.29.20.

P10-013.challenge_claim: First item: the discourse-imperative summons one verse before the front seam is a stronger, undisclosed rival for this unit's opening. Second item: the koh-amar the seam rests on is never quoted in the original language, its mouth and written medium are unnamed, a single-site name-form change inside the span is undisclosed, and a paseq seg in the span is undisclosed.
P10-013.grounds: The two items are distinct and both stand. Rival onset: oshb:Jer.29.20 opens וְאַתֶּ֖ם שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה (byte tier), the plural hear-the-word-of-YHWH summons with a vocative naming the exiles - a recurring book-wide shape (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton tier) standing immediately after a doubled verse-final closure formula at 29:19 and followed at once by the oracle this unit carries - while the disclosed alternative weighs only whether the curse formula of verse 22 should split from verse 21, and never whether that summons belongs forward as this unit's opening. The comparison to the summons cited from elsewhere in the book holds as a class parallel and not as a byte recurrence: the two needles differ at skeleton tier. Evidence mechanics: oshb:Jer.29.21 opens כֹּֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (byte tier) verse-initially, and the row's own pointed run begins after it at אֶל אַחְאָ֤ב בֶּן קֽוֹלָיָה֙, so the device carrying the seam is quoted in the other witness alone, against the standing requirement that a boundary-relevant original-language claim be spliced with its tier named. Ownership and medium are unnamed in the one stretch where formulas stand inside a quoted letter and, one chapter earlier, in a false prophet's mouth; the field's signal keys carry the speech formula alone with no letter-frame key, although the units at 29:4-29:14 and at 29:24-29:29 both declare that frame for the same document. The name-form change is byte-real and load-bearing on the row's own rejection: the fuller spelling אַחְאָ֤ב stands at 29:21 and the shorter base וּכְאֶחָ֔ב one verse later at 29:22 (byte tier; skeleton sweeps, finals-normalized: 1 verse each, book-wide), so the sentence binding verse 22 back to verse 21 by name rests on two different attested spellings without saying so. One paseq seg stands at MT 29:21 inside the span, undisclosed, while both parashah marks and the ketiv/qere and exegesis note at MT 29:23 are disclosed. What verifies: the resh-family royal spelling at 29:21 and its contrast with the nun-family forms at 29:1 and 29:3 are byte-true, and both setumah citations match the inventory under their types.

row.boundary_rationale: A claim quoted from the exiles’ own mouths opens the unit, כִּ֖י אֲמַרְתֶּ֑ם (oshb:Jer.29.15, byte), matching “Because you have said,” (web:Jer.29.15) — a setumah falls in this same opening verse. The address then turns to a party the letter has not yet named directly, כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֶל הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ הַיּוֹשֵׁב֙ אֶל כִּסֵּ֣א דָוִ֔ד וְאֶל כָּל הָעָ֔ם הַיּוֹשֵׁ֖ב בָּעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֑את אֲחֵיכֶ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא יָצְא֥וּ אִתְּכֶ֖ם בַּגּוֹלָֽה (oshb:Jer.29.16, byte), matching “Yahweh says concerning the king who sits on David’s throne, and concerning all the people who dwell in this city, your brothers who haven’t gone with you into captivity,” (web:Jer.29.16) — the king on David’s throne and the people who stayed in Jerusalem, rather than the exiles the letter actually addresses. Judgment against them continues through verse 18, matching “I will pursue after them with the sword, with the famine, and with the pestilence, and will deliver them to be tossed back and forth among all the kingdoms of the earth, to be an object of horror, an astonishment, a hissing, and a reproach among all the nations where I have driven them,” (web:Jer.29.18); a ketiv/qere note sits in this same verse, on the word for horror itself: ketiv לזועה against qere לְזַעֲוָ֜ה (oshb:Jer.29.18, WLC, single-witness). It closes on a summons back to the letter’s own audience, וְאַתֶּ֖ם שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה כָּל הַ֨גּוֹלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר שִׁלַּ֥חְתִּי מִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה (oshb:Jer.29.20, byte), matching “Hear therefore Yahweh’s word, all you captives whom I have sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon.” (web:Jer.29.20) — a setumah also falls in this closing verse. Whether verse 15’s quoted claim belongs with the settle-in promise that precedes it or with the Jerusalem judgment it introduces is not settled by any formula; it is read here with what follows, since the address it opens is answered only by the turn to the king and the city at verse 16. A fresh koh-amar names two further parties directly at verse 21, Ahab and Zedekiah, so this row is bounded just short of that naming.
row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading verse 15 as the closing verse of the settle-in and restoration unit that precedes it, rather than as the opening of the Jerusalem judgment that follows, was seriously considered and is not decided here: no formula marks which side of the seam it belongs on, and the row is held at reduced confidence honestly rather than resolving that question either way.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The letter’s own quoted content opens on the full title stack, כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְכָל הַ֨גּוֹלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר הִגְלֵ֥יתִי מִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה (oshb:Jer.29.4, byte), matching “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says to all the captives whom I have caused to be carried away captive from Jerusalem to Babylon:” (web:Jer.29.4), addressed to all the exiles by name for the first time in the letter. Settle-in instructions follow at once, בְּנ֥וּ בָתִּ֖ים וְשֵׁ֑בוּ וְנִטְע֣וּ גַנּ֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.29.5, byte), matching “Build houses and dwell in them. Plant gardens and eat their fruit.” (web:Jer.29.5). A further koh-amar recurs at verse 8, turning from settling in to a warning against the exiles’ own prophets and diviners, and a third recurs at verse 10, כִּֽי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֠י לְפִ֞י מְלֹ֧את לְבָבֶ֛ל שִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה אֶפְקֹ֣ד (oshb:Jer.29.10, byte), matching “After seventy years are accomplished for Babylon, I will visit you and perform my good word toward you, in causing you to return to this place.” (web:Jer.29.10) — a promise of return after seventy years; none of these internal recurrences carries a change of speaker or a fresh addressee of its own, so all three turns are held inside one continuous letter-address to the same audience rather than cut into separate rows. It closes on “and I will turn again your captivity, and I will gather you from all the nations, and from all the places where I have driven you,” (web:Jer.29.14); a ketiv/qere note sits in this same closing verse, on the word for captivity itself: ketiv שביתכם against qere שְׁבוּתְכֶ֗ם (oshb:Jer.29.14, WLC, single-witness). The address turns from Yahweh’s own promise to a claim quoted from the exiles’ own mouths at verse 15, marking the far edge of this row.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting fresh rows at the koh-amar recurrences opening verses 8 and 10 was considered, since each turns to a distinct topic within the letter — the false prophets, then the seventy-year promise — but rejected because none carries a frame-owner change or an addressee shift of its own; the whole eleven-verse span remains one sustained address from Yahweh to the same exile audience, held together honestly rather than split on topic alone.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar names two further parties directly for the first time, אֶל אַחְאָ֤ב בֶּן קֽוֹלָיָה֙ וְאֶל צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בֶן מַֽעֲשֵׂיָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.29.21, byte), matching “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says concerning Ahab the son of Kolaiah, and concerning Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, who prophesy a lie to you in my name:” (web:Jer.29.21) — Ahab and Zedekiah, prophesying falsely in Yahweh’s name among the exiles themselves. Their sentence names the king who will kill them, בְּיַד֙ נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר (oshb:Jer.29.21, byte) — a resh-family spelling of Nebuchadnezzar’s name, distinct from the nun-family forms spelled earlier in this same letter at oshb:Jer.29.1 and oshb:Jer.29.3. The unit continues through the curse formula built on both their names and closes on the rationale for the sentence, יַ֡עַן אֲשֶׁר֩ עָשׂ֨וּ נְבָלָ֜ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיְנַֽאֲפוּ֙ אֶת נְשֵׁ֣י רֵֽעֵיהֶ֔ם וַיְדַבְּר֨וּ דָבָ֤ר בִּשְׁמִי֙ שֶׁ֔קֶר אֲשֶׁ֖ר ל֣וֹא צִוִּיתִ֑ם וְאָנֹכִ֛י (oshb:Jer.29.23, byte), matching “because they have done foolish things in Israel, and have committed adultery with their neighbors’ wives, and have spoken words in my name falsely, which I didn’t command them. I am he who knows, and am witness,” (web:Jer.29.23); a ketiv/qere note sits in this same closing verse: ketiv הו ידע against qere הַיּוֹדֵ֥עַ (oshb:Jer.29.23, WLC, single-witness), alongside a separate OSHB exegesis note at the same verse (single-witness apparatus, not text bytes). The address turns to a third, differently-named figure at verse 24, Shemaiah the Nehelamite, which is where this row ends.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A third named figure opens the unit, וְאֶל שְׁמַעְיָ֥הוּ הַנֶּחֱלָמִ֖י תֹּאמַ֥ר לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.29.24, byte), matching “Concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite you shall speak, saying,” (web:Jer.29.24) — Shemaiah the Nehelamite, commissioned as the subject of Jeremiah’s own reply rather than addressed directly. The reply quotes Shemaiah’s own hostile letter back at him, including its rebuke naming Jeremiah by his home village, בְּיִרְמְיָ֖הוּ הָֽעֲנְּתֹתִ֑י (oshb:Jer.29.27, byte), matching “Now therefore, why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who makes himself a prophet to you,” (web:Jer.29.27) — a defective spelling of the gentilic naming that village. It closes on a narrative report explaining how this exchange became known, וַיִּקְרָ֛א צְפַנְיָ֥ה הַכֹּהֵ֖ן אֶת הַסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֑ה בְּאָזְנֵ֖י יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִֽיא (oshb:Jer.29.29, byte), matching “Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the hearing of Jeremiah the prophet.” (web:Jer.29.29). A fresh word-event formula opens at verse 30, turning from this narrative report to Yahweh’s own word to Jeremiah, and the row does not extend past that opening.

P11-002.challenge_claim: Two items, distinct defects. (i) The unit's own opening quotation, the messenger formula the row relies on as its seam warrant, is glossed in English only from partway through the Hebrew verse spliced beside it at Jer.30.5. (ii) The declared false-positive disposition is refuted: Jer.30.8 carries the span's first second-person singular addressee, so the asserted absence of an addressee change at that turn is byte-false in both witnesses.
P11-002.grounds: Both upheld; distinct defects, one mechanical and one substantive. (i) The 30:5 pair splices the whole verse including כִּי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.30.5, byte) but glosses only from the cry onward, while the staged verse opens “For Yahweh says:” (web:Jer.30.5) — the formula's own English stands in the same staged verse and is left uncovered, on the single device the row cites as its opening warrant. (ii) Person marking re-derived across the span: 30:5 carries the first-person plural שָׁמָ֑עְנוּ, 30:6 the second-person plural שַׁאֲלוּ נָ֣א וּרְא֔וּ, 30:7 third person throughout, and then 30:8 carries אֶשְׁבֹּ֤ר עֻלּוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל צַוָּארֶ֔ךָ וּמוֹסְרוֹתֶ֖יךָ אֲנַתֵּ֑ק (oshb:Jer.30.5, oshb:Jer.30.6, oshb:Jer.30.8, byte for each), the span's first second-person singular marking, rendered the same way in the other witness, “that I will break his yoke from off your neck, and will burst your bonds.” (web:Jer.30.8). A flat denial that any addressee change marks that turn is byte-false. Two calibration points that do not disturb the finding but do bear on how strong the rival is. First, that marking is sustained to the row's own close, וְאַתָּ֡ה אַל תִּירָא֩ עַבְדִּ֨י (oshb:Jer.30.10, byte) and כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י through אֲנַקֶּֽךָּ (oshb:Jer.30.11, byte for each), so this is a turn into a sustained address rather than a one-verse anomaly. Second, the 30:8 clause mixes persons in one breath, עֻלּוֹ֙ third-person beside צַוָּארֶ֔ךָ second-person (oshb:Jer.30.8, byte for each), so the turn is a person shift inside continuous divine speech, not a clean fresh address. A precision note on the framing, not a correction to the finding: the flagged word in that sentence is a restrictive adverb and is a genuine keyword false positive on its own terms; what fails is the absence clause standing beside it. Everything else verifies: no mark at MT 30:4, SAMEKH at MT 30:9, PE at MT 30:11, one paseq seg each at MT 30:8 and MT 30:11 (single-witness, count-only), no ketiv/qere; the hoy at 30:7 is the day-alas role and not a woe onset; the Jacob spelling is defective at 30:7 and twice at 30:10 (sweep: 2 token hits at Jer.30.10, 1 prefixed at Jer.30.7, skeleton, finals-normalized) against the plene form at 30:18; and all five pointed runs and all five English runs are byte-true and verbatim respectively.

Re-argue the rejection on grounds the bytes support — state the second-person singular entry at 30:8, weigh it against the mixed person marking inside that same clause and against the absence of any fresh speech formula there, and land the rejection on that. The day named next carries the hoy interjection in its own DAY-ALAS shape, not a woe-oracle onset: ה֗וֹי כִּ֥י גָד֛וֹל הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא מֵאַ֣יִן כָּמֹ֑הוּ וְעֵֽת צָרָ֥ה הִיא֙ לְיַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וּמִמֶּ֖נָּה יִוָּשֵֽׁעַ (oshb:Jer.30.7, byte), matching “Alas, for that day is great, so that none is like it! It is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he will be saved out of it.” (web:Jer.30.7) — an exclamation over the day's own severity rather than a pronounced judgment against a named party, closing already on the promise of rescue rather than on threat alone. Jacob's name in this same verse carries the defective spelling these bytes attest. A day-formula turn follows at verse 8 without any addressee change, וְהָיָה֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא נְאֻ֣ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת אֶשְׁבֹּ֤ר עֻלּוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל צַוָּארֶ֔ךָ וּמוֹסְרוֹתֶ֖יךָ אֲנַתֵּ֑ק וְלֹא יַעַבְדוּ ב֥וֹ ע֖וֹד זָרִֽים (oshb:Jer.30.8, byte), matching “It will come to pass in that day, says Yahweh of Armies, that I will break his yoke from off your neck, and will burst your bonds. Strangers will no more make them their bondservants;” (web:Jer.30.8); a full neum-YHWH-tsevaot stack sits inside this same verse, corroborating rather than opening a fresh unit, since no koh-amar or addressee shift accompanies it. The rescue promise continues through the same defective spelling of Jacob's name twice over, וְאַתָּ֡ה אַל תִּירָא֩ עַבְדִּ֨י יַעֲקֹ֤ב נְאֻם יְהֹוָה֙ וְאַל תֵּחַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֠י הִנְנִ֤י מוֹשִֽׁיעֲךָ֙ מֵֽרָח֔וֹק וְאֶֽת זַרְעֲךָ֖ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ שִׁבְיָ֑ם וְשָׁ֧ב יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְשָׁקַ֥ט וְשַׁאֲנַ֖ן וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד (oshb:Jer.30.10, byte), matching “Therefore don’t be afraid, O Jacob my servant, says Yahweh. Don’t be dismayed, Israel. For, behold, I will save you from afar, and save your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return, and will be quiet and at ease. No one will make him afraid.” (web:Jer.30.10). It closes on כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י נְאֻם יְהוָ֖ה לְהֽוֹשִׁיעֶ֑ךָ כִּי֩ אֶעֱשֶׂ֨ה כָלָ֜ה בְּכָֽל הַגּוֹיִ֣ם אֲשֶׁ֧ר הֲפִצוֹתִ֣יךָ שָּׁ֗ם אַ֤ךְ אֹֽתְךָ֙ לֹֽא אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה כָלָ֔ה וְיִסַּרְתִּ֨יךָ֙ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט וְנַקֵּ֖ה לֹ֥א אֲנַקֶּֽךָּ (oshb:Jer.30.11, byte), matching “For I am with you, says Yahweh, to save you; for I will make a full end of all the nations where I have scattered you, but I will not make a full end of you; but I will correct you in measure, and will in no way leave you unpunished.” (web:Jer.30.11). A command to write follows without any change of speaker, כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר כְּתָב לְךָ֗ אֵ֧ת כָּל הַדְּבָרִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי אֵלֶ֖יךָ אֶל סֵֽפֶר (oshb:Jer.30.2, byte), matching “Yahweh, the God of Israel, says, ‘Write all the words that I have spoken to you in a book.” (web:Jer.30.2) — write every word spoken into a book. The content commanded to be written follows at once, closing on the promise itself: כִּ֠י הִנֵּ֨ה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה וְ֠שַׁבְתִּי אֶת שְׁב֨וּת עַמִּ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וִֽיהוּדָ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֗ים אֶל הָאָ֛רֶץ אֲשֶׁר נָתַ֥תִּי לַאֲבוֹתָ֖ם וִֽירֵשֽׁוּהָ (oshb:Jer.30.3, byte), matching “For, behold, the days come,’ says Yahweh, ‘that I will reverse the captivity of my people Israel and Judah,’ says Yahweh. ‘I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they will possess it.’” (web:Jer.30.3). A third-person rubric then names what has just been given, וְאֵ֣לֶּה הַדְּבָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְאֶל יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.30.4, byte), matching “These are the words that Yahweh spoke concerning Israel and concerning Judah.” (web:Jer.30.4) — dropping out of quoted divine speech into the narrator's own summary of it. Nothing between the header and this rubric reopens the address with a new addressee or discourse imperative, so the whole four-verse frame stands as one unit. A fresh koh-amar opens the first poem at verse 5, matching “For Yahweh says: ” (web:Jer.30.5), and this row stops short of that onset.

(ii) The declared false-positive disposition is refuted: Jer.31.2 has no addressee at all and Jer.31.3 both reports the deity in the third person and opens a feminine-singular address, so the asserted single continuous voice addressed to one figure is byte-false.
P11-005.grounds: Both upheld, and they interlock rather than duplicate. (i) The 31:2 pair splices the whole verse including כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.31.2, byte) and glosses only from the wilderness clause onward, while the staged verse opens “Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.31.2) — again the uncovered element is the unit's own opening seam device. The 31:3 pair splices the whole verse including מֵרָח֕וֹק יְהוָ֖ה נִרְאָ֣ה לִ֑י (oshb:Jer.31.3, byte) and glosses only from the love clause onward, leaving “Yahweh appeared of old to me, saying,” (web:Jer.31.3) uncovered. (ii) MT 31:2 carries no second-person form anywhere: מָצָ֥א and הָל֥וֹךְ לְהַרְגִּיע֖וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Jer.31.2, byte for each) are third person throughout, so there is no addressed figure at 31:2 for 31:3 to keep addressing. MT 31:3 then opens by naming the divine name in the third person beside a first-person singular pronoun, מֵרָח֕וֹק יְהוָ֖ה נִרְאָ֣ה לִ֑י (oshb:Jer.31.3, byte), read the same way in the other witness, and only after that clause do the feminine-singular forms אֲהַבְתִּ֔יךְ and מְשַׁכְתִּ֥יךְ (oshb:Jer.31.3, byte for each) begin. The asserted single continuous voice addressed to the same figure fails on both halves. The consistency point holds too: the same feminine-singular pointing that carries an onset warrant at אָנ֣וּשׁ לְשִׁבְרֵ֑ךְ (oshb:Jer.30.12, byte) is refused that weight here, one device read two ways within six verses. The two items interlock: the clause the quotation leaves uncovered at 31:3 is precisely the clause that falsifies the rejection sentence, so curing the pairing surfaces the evidence against the row's own stated ground. Disclosures verify: SAMEKH at MT 31:1 at the front seam, PE at MT 31:6 at the close, no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note in the span; the 31:4 and 31:6 pairs are extent-clean, and all four pointed runs are byte-true with all four English runs verbatim.

Test the cure the way the original failed: read the rewritten sentence back against oshb:Jer.31.2 and oshb:Jer.31.3 and confirm it asserts no person or addressee continuity the bytes deny; and if feminine-singular onset marking is refused weight here, the refusal must rest on a ground that does not contradict the weight the same pointing is given at Jer.30.12. The same voice continues in direct declaration, מֵרָח֕וֹק יְהוָ֖ה נִרְאָ֣ה לִ֑י וְאַהֲבַ֤ת עוֹלָם֙ אֲהַבְתִּ֔יךְ עַל כֵּ֖ן מְשַׁכְתִּ֥יךְ חָֽסֶד (oshb:Jer.31.3, byte), matching “Yes, I have loved you with an everlasting love. Therefore I have drawn you with loving kindness.” (web:Jer.31.3). Rebuilding imagery follows, ע֤וֹד אֶבְנֵךְ֙ וְֽנִבְנֵ֔ית בְּתוּלַ֖ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ע֚וֹד תַּעְדִּ֣י תֻפַּ֔יִךְ וְיָצָ֖את בִּמְח֥וֹל מְשַׂחֲקִֽים (oshb:Jer.31.4, byte), matching “I will build you again, and you will be built, O virgin of Israel. You will again be adorned with your tambourines, and will go out in the dances of those who make merry.” (web:Jer.31.4) — virgin Israel, tambourines, dances. P11-012.challenge_claim: One item: the back boundary is argued only from a recurring days-are-coming incipit absent from the book's tier-1 seam catalog, and the unit's own test for declining a cut at verse 29 applies just as directly to verse 31 without being engaged. The other item: the stated ground for holding verses 29-30 with verses 27-28 is byte-false because the divine first-person voice does not continue past verse 28, and the front-seam device is a widely recurring shape carried without a digit and with a third chapter-internal site undisclosed.
P11-012.grounds: The two items are distinct in target - one goes to the back-seam warrant and to consistency with the declined internal cut, the other to the rejected alternative's stated ground and to the front-seam device's digit - but they converge on one underlying defect: the row's description of the voice pattern across oshb:Jer.31.27 to oshb:Jer.31.31. Upheld: the rejected alternative's ground is byte-false. The first two verses of the span carry divine first-person forms - וְזָרַעְתִּ֗י (oshb:Jer.31.27, byte), שָׁקַ֣דְתִּי and אֶשְׁקֹ֧ד (oshb:Jer.31.28, byte) - while the last two carry none: לֹא יֹאמְר֣וּ ע֔וֹד (oshb:Jer.31.29, byte) and אִ֥ישׁ בַּעֲוֺנ֖וֹ יָמ֑וּת ... תִּקְהֶ֥ינָה שִׁנָּֽיו (oshb:Jer.31.30, byte) are third-person throughout, and both witnesses render them so. Upheld: the front-seam device is typed a refrain and ships with no digit; the shape stands in 15 verses book-wide at the consonantal tier and 5 at byte tier (MT keys), three of them in this chapter - oshb:Jer.31.27, oshb:Jer.31.31 and oshb:Jer.31.38 - and the third site is undisclosed. Recurrence at that density does not by itself found a unit. Upheld: quote-gloss parity. All four splices are whole verses and byte-verbatim, but the renderings cover 15, 93, 67 and 100 percent; the 67 percent pair drops the head that renders בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם (oshb:Jer.31.29, byte), the very clause the rejected alternative is about, and the 15 percent pair leaves a sixteen-word splice glossed by four rendered words. Refined: the back-seam framing does not survive re-derivation. The seam is under-STATED, not under-warranted - the third-person proverb material gives way to divine first person at וְכָרַתִּ֗י (oshb:Jer.31.31, byte), a person shift absent at the internal seam the row declines. The parity argument asserts that the same first-person divine voice stands on both sides of the back seam; the bytes refute that in exactly the way the row's own sentence is refuted, so that argument reproduces the defect it is charging. Also refined: the incipit's absence from the enumerated internal-cut classes is real, but the back seam does not rest on the incipit alone once the bytes are read, and a byte-true ground for holding the proverb material with what precedes is available and unused - the declined verse opens בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם (oshb:Jer.31.29, byte), anaphoric to the days named at the span's own opening verse. Verified in the row's favour: the incipit is verse-initial and byte-exact at oshb:Jer.31.27; the setumah pair at the front-seam verse and the closing verse is exact (single-witness, tier-3 weak); the inventory records no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note inside the span; the proverb material is engaged from the bytes with no cross-tradition appeal.

P14-008.grounds: The bytes carry it. The last speech introduction before the seam is וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ (oshb:Jer.38.20, byte). MT 38:21 then opens וְאִם מָאֵ֥ן אַתָּ֖ה לָצֵ֑את (oshb:Jer.38.21, byte) - a waw-conditional, with no speech introduction, no addressee change, no narrative frame and no dated notice. The verse runs to nine words entire, so the account is exhaustive: nothing in the pointed text marks a unit onset there. A conditional series straddles the junction: אִם יָצֹ֨א תֵצֵ֜א (oshb:Jer.38.17, byte), then וְאִ֣ם לֹֽא תֵצֵ֗א (oshb:Jer.38.18, byte), then MT 38:21's third protasis on the same exit verb. A byte-true construction straddling a unit's own junction argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed, and no field discloses it. One refinement of the framing that strengthens rather than weakens the finding: MT 38:17-38:18 belong to an earlier turn of the same speaker, interrupted by the king at MT 38:19, while MT 38:21 sits inside the turn opened at MT 38:20 - so the series runs across two of Jeremiah's turns, and the seam itself falls inside one of them, which is the fact that kills the cut. The showing formula does not carry the seam either. הִרְאַ֖נִי stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses - 24:1, 38:21). At 24:1 the formula is the verse's own opening, הִרְאַנִי֮ יְהוָה֒ (oshb:Jer.24.1, byte); at 38:21 it is verse-medial, standing behind the conditional. So the device note's plural reference to the book's formal vision reports overstates a form with one other site, carries no digit, and the same note concedes that the showing is embedded inside an ongoing address rather than standing as a separate report - which withdraws the only warrant offered for the cut. The mark layer offers no corroboration at this junction: marks key MT 38:19 and MT 38:23, not MT 38:20 (single-witness, tier-3 weak; stated as non-corroboration only, since absence is never counterevidence). The lesser point also holds: the poetic-lines characterisation of verse 22 rests on the modern line layout of the English, which is tier-4 and never evidence in either direction, and it carries no tier label. High severity is right: once the warrant is withdrawn, the seam has no surviving tier-1 signal standing in its own onset verse. The unit's closing junction is not in question - the petuchah keyed to MT 38:23 sits at it, no ketiv/qere note or paseq seg falls in Jer.38.21-Jer.38.23, and both pointed splices reach byte tier.
P14-008.remedy: Two parts, and the boundary part is a PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption - never author work.
